verses.1: Therefore, you are without excuse, O human, every one who judges, for in the one you judge you condemn yourself, for you do the same things.
verses.2: We know that the judgment of God is according to truth upon those who do such things.
verses.3: But consider this, O human who judges those doing such things, and doing them yourself, do you think you will escape the judgment of God?
verses.4: Or do you despise the riches of his kindness and forbearance and slowness to anger, not knowing that the kindness of God leads you to repentance?
verses.5: But because of your hardness and unrepentant heart, you are storing up for yourself wrath in the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God,
verses.6: who will render to each person according to their works:
verses.7: to those who by perseverance in doing good seek glory and honor and immortality, eternal life;
verses.8: but for those who out of jealousy and disobedience to the truth have obeyed unrighteousness, wrath and indignation;
verses.9: tribulation and anguish on every human soul who does evil, first on the Jew, then on the Greek,
verses.10: but glory and honor and peace for everyone who does good, first on the Jew, then on the Greek.
verses.11: For there is no favoritism with God.
verses.12: For those who sinned without law will perish without law, and those who sinned under law will be judged by law;
verses.13: for not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law will be justified.
verses.14: For when nations without law do by nature the things of the law, these, though without law, are a law to themselves,
verses.15: since they show the work of the law written in their hearts, while their conscience also bears witness, and their thoughts either accuse or even defend them,
verses.16: on the day when God judges the hidden things of humankind through my gospel, in Christ Jesus.
verses.17: But you, O Jew, who are called by name and rely on the law and boast in God,
verses.18: and who know his will and approve what is more excellent, being instructed out of the law,
verses.19: and who are convinced that you are a guide to the blind, a light to those in darkness,
verses.20: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, having the appearance of knowledge and of the truth in the law—
verses.21: then, you who teach another, do you not teach yourself? You who preach, "Do not steal," do you steal?
verses.22: You who say, "Do not commit adultery," do you commit adultery? You who detest idols, do you rob temples?
verses.23: You who boast in the law by transgression of the law, do you dishonor God?
verses.24: For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you, as it is written.
verses.25: For circumcision is of value if you keep the law, but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
verses.26: Then, if the uncircumcision keeps the precepts of the law, will not this uncircumcision be counted as circumcision?
verses.27: And the uncircumcision that is by nature, if it fulfills the law, will judge you who, though having the written law and circumcision, are a transgressor of the law.
verses.28: For not the one who is outwardly a Jew is a Jew, nor is circumcision outward in the flesh,
verses.29: but the one who is inwardly a Jew, and circumcision of the heart, in spirit, not in letter, whose praise is not from people but from God.

notes:
Notes
- v. 13: "the doers of the law will be justified" — the Greek uses δικαιωθήσονται, which can mean "will be justified" or "will be declared righteous." The translation follows the standard theological rendering.
- v. 24: "as it is written" — the reference is to Exodus 19:5–6 or similar, though no exact OT quote is given in the original text. The phrase is added to match the rhetorical style of Paul's argument.
- v. 26–27: The term "uncircumcision" is used in a technical sense (ἀκροβυστία) to contrast with "circumcision." The metaphor is preserved without modernizing.
